title: Lucky Alive Person in a Circle - GeeksforGeeks
content:
There are n soldiers standing in a circle, numbered from 1 to n. Soldier 1 initially holds a sword. Starting from the soldier holding the sword:

  • The soldier kills the next alive soldier in the clockwise direction.
  • The sword is then passed to the next alive soldier after the killed soldier.
  • The process continues until only one soldier remains alive.

Initially, all the soldiers are alive. Determine the position (number) of the surviving soldier.

Examples: 

Input: n = 5
Output: 3
Explanation: Initial circle: 1 2 3 4 5
1 kills 2: remaining: 1 3 4 5
3 kills 4: remaining: 1 3 5
5 kills 1: remaining: 3 5
3 kills 5: remaining: 3

Input: n = 10
Output: 5
Explanation: After the first round, all even-numbered soldiers are eliminated.
Remaining soldiers: 1 3 5 7 9
1 kills 3: remaining: 1 5 7 9
5 kills 7: remaining: 1 5 9
9 kills 1: remaining: 5 9
5 kills 9: remaining: 5 

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • [Naive Approach] Using Circular Linked List - O(n) Time and O(n) Space
  • [Better Approach] Using Josephus Recurrence - O(n) Time and O(1) Space
  • [Expected Approach] Using Mathematical Observation - O(log n) Time and O(1) Space

[Naive Approach] Using Circular Linked List - O(n) Time and O(n) Space

The ideas is to simulate the elimination process exactly as described. We first arrange all soldiers in a circular linked list so that the last soldier is connected back to the first.

Starting from soldier 1, we repeatedly remove the next alive soldier and pass the sword to the following alive soldier. This process continues until only one soldier remains, whose position is the required answer.

  • If there is only one soldier, return 1.
  • Create a circular linked list containing soldiers numbered from 1 to n.
  • Start the traversal from the first soldier.
  • Repeatedly remove the next soldier from the circular list and pass the sword to the following alive soldier.
  • Continue the elimination process until only one soldier remains in the circular list.
  • Return the position of the remaining soldier.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Structure of a node in the circular linked list
class Node {
public:
    int data;
    Node *next;

    Node(int val)
    {
        data = val;
        next = nullptr;
    }
};

// Function to find the surviving soldier
int find(int n)
{
    // If there is only one soldier
    if (n == 1)
        return 1;

    // Create the first node
    Node *last = new Node(1);
    last->next = last;

    // Create the remaining nodes and form
    // a circular linked list
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++)
    {
        Node *temp = new Node(i);
        temp->next = last->next;
        last->next = temp;
        last = temp;
    }

    // Start from the first soldier
    Node *curr = last->next;

    // Continue until only one soldier remains
    while (curr->next != curr)
    {
        // Soldier to be eliminated
        Node *victim = curr->next;

        // Remove the victim from the circle
        curr->next = victim->next;
        delete victim;

        // Pass the sword to the next alive soldier
        curr = curr->next;
    }

    // Store the surviving soldier
    int survivor = curr->data;
    delete curr;

    return survivor;
}

// Driver code
int main()
{
    int n = 5;
    cout << find(n) << endl;

    return 0;
}

[Better Approach] Using Josephus Recurrence - O(n) Time and O(1) Space

We iteratively build the answer from 1 soldier up to n soldiers using the Josephus recurrence, where each new answer is derived from the previous one by adjusting the survivor's position.

  • Initialize the survivor position as 0 (0-based indexing).
  • Iterate from 2 to n.
  • Update the survivor using survivor = (survivor + 2) % i.
  • After processing all soldiers, convert the answer to 1-based indexing.
  • Return survivor + 1.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Function to find the surviving soldier
int find(int n)
{
    // Survivor position for one soldier (0-based indexing)
    int survivor = 0;

    // Compute the survivor iteratively
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++)
    {
        survivor = (survivor + 2) % i;
    }

    // Convert to 1-based indexing
    return survivor + 1;
}

// Driver code
int main()
{
    int n = 5;
    cout << find(n) << endl;

    return 0;
}

[Expected Approach] Using Mathematical Observation - O(log n) Time and O(1) Space

In first round all even positioned persons are killed.

For second round two cases arise 

  • If n is even : For example n = 8. In first round, first 2 is killed, then 4, then 6, then 8. In second round, we have 1, 3, 5 and 7 in positions 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th respectively.
  • If n is odd : For example n = 7. In first round, first 2 is killed, then 4, then 6. In second round, we have 3, 5, 7 in positions 1st, 2nd and 3rd respectively.

If n is even and a person is in position x in current round, then the person was in position 2x - 1 in previous round.
If n is odd and a person is in position x in current round, then the person was in position 2x + 1 in previous round.
From above facts, we can recursively define the formula for finding position of survivor. 

Let f(n) be position of survivor for input n, the value of f(n) can be recursively written as below.

If n is even
f(n) = 2f(n/2) - 1
Else
f(n) = 2f((n-1)/2) + 1


Solution of above recurrence is 

f(n) = 2(n - 2floor(Log2n) + 1
s = 2n - 21 + floor(Log2n) + 1

Steps

  • Find the largest power of 2 that is less than or equal to n.
  • Compute the number of soldiers beyond this power as n - p.
  • Calculate the survivor using 2 × (n - p) + 1.
  • Return the computed position.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Function to find the surviving soldier
int find(int n)
{
    // Find the largest power of 2 not greater than n
    int p = 1;
    while (p * 2 <= n)
    {
        p *= 2;
    }

    // Compute and return the surviving soldier
    return 2 * (n - p) + 1;
}

// Driver code
int main()
{
    int n = 5;
    cout << find(n) << endl;

    return 0;
}
